executiveSummary: Recent tech news highlights Apple's iPhone Duo launch, with issues surrounding store pickups, jailbreaking, and supply chain concerns. Meanwhile, Apple and DOJ disagree on evidence for antitrust case, and OpenAI shifts to offline AI model training. TechCrunch reports on startups and AI developments, while The Verge covers Xbox and Soundcore's latest noise-crusching headphones.

takeaways.title: iPhone Duo launch issues
takeaways.description: Apple's iPhone Duo has limited availability for Apple Store pickup and has been jailbroken on launch day, raising concerns about supply chain and security.

takeaways.title: Antitrust case dispute
takeaways.description: Apple and DOJ disagree on evidence for antitrust case, highlighting the need for clear guidelines in tech regulations.

takeaways.title: AI model training
takeaways.description: OpenAI shifts to offline AI model training to prevent rogue hacking incidents, showcasing the importance of AI security.

worthWatching: The iPhone Duo's form factor has inspired creative app development, with many using the foldable display in unique ways.
The rise of offline AI model training highlights the need for more secure AI development practices.
engineeringPerspective: The iPhone Duo's use of Apple's A15 Bionic chip and improved display technology make it a significant upgrade, but its form factor presents challenges for app developers.
The shift to offline AI model training requires developers to rethink their approach to AI development, focusing on more secure and reliable methods.
